title: Honest Adaptive Intervals for the Optimal Policy Value under Ties and Near Ties
banked_reason: User-directed D0 pipeline test completed normally after three solve rounds; the sound subfield result was intentionally stopped with five gated proposals and two open obligations still pending.
gap_reasons: tier=letter below novelty_target=field: the core reuses the published softmax orthogonal-score route and supplies neither a matched causal adaptation frontier, a strict rate/constant improvement over a named result, nor a first published-method bound; finite-union uniformization alone is not yet a demonstrated Stat frontier advance.
The exact matching union-honest interval and the sharp frontier boundary remained open obligations when the user-directed D0 test stopped.
proof_attempt_summary: The proposal loop repaired the full-data model, literature positioning, causal least-favorable construction, and phase-boundary algebra before the run was deliberately advanced to D0 for pipeline testing. D0 completed three persisted solve rounds, discharged and rendered the initial theorem package, then correctly gated statement/core changes and preserved provisional proofs rather than auto-applying them. The matching union-honest upper interval and exact expected-length frontier remain open, so the result is banked as a retryable subfield contribution rather than a field-level matched adaptation theorem.
tldr: Under iid sampling, known one-half randomization, bounded outcomes, Hölder outcome regressions, and a margin condition that permits a tie atom, a sparse randomized-sign experiment forces every union-honest connected interval for the optimal policy value to have expected length at least \(n^{-1/2}\vee n^{-\xi}\) at the exact-tie base law, where \(\xi=2s_1(\alpha+1)/(d+s_1\alpha+4s_1)\). The explicit split-sample learned-policy interval \(C_n^\dagger\) is uniformly honest and has length \(O(n^{-1/2}+n^{-\rho})\), where \(\rho=s_1(\alpha+1)/(2s_1+d)\). These scales coincide at root \(n\) when \(2s_1\alpha\ge d\); outside that subregime, attainment of the sparse lower scale by the distinct hypothetical multiscale interval \(C_n^{\mathrm{ms}}\) remains open.
gap: Existing inference for exceptional optimal-treatment laws does not provide this two-stratum expected-length adaptation diagram for a connected interval that is honest simultaneously over exact ties and Hölder near ties with an allowed tie atom. The unresolved issue is sharply localized: when \(2s_1\alpha<d\), the proved lower exponent \(\min\{1/2,\xi\}\) and achievable exponent \(\min\{1/2,\rho\}\) differ.
fill: The lower calculation holds for every admissible pair; the inequality \(3s_1\alpha<d\) is needed only for the corollary that the sparse scale is strictly slower than root \(n\). Combining that calculation with a parametric tie submodel gives the unified lower scale \(n^{-1/2}\vee n^{-\xi}\) on both strata. The proved split-sample interval \(C_n^\dagger\) supplies the honest upper scale \(n^{-1/2}+n^{-\rho}\); the symbol \(C_n^{\mathrm{ms}}\) is reserved for the unresolved multiscale route.
